title: std.time.nanoTimestamp missing on x86_64-macos target (2 call sites)
registered_by: Found while fixing ISS-0134 (Linux Environ portability); verified via cross-compile
scope: macOS cross-compilation only. No impact on Linux CI or Windows development.
symptom: zig build -Dtarget=x86_64-macos fails with 2 errors: std.time.nanoTimestamp has no member on this target, in src/admin/tenant_migration.zig:685 and src/api/routes/onboarding.zig:24. Both are @intCast(std.time.nanoTimestamp()) in the non-Windows fallback branch of a PRNG seed helper. Confirmed this is macOS-specific, not a general POSIX gap: -Dtarget=x86_64-linux-gnu and -Dtarget=aarch64-linux-gnu both compile the identical lines cleanly.
root_cause_analysis: std.time has no timestamp API at all in Zig 0.16.0 (verified against the installed toolchain's lib/std/time.zig — only duration constants remain). Timestamps moved behind std.Io.Clock.now(io, clock), which requires an Io instance neither fillRandom() helper has access to. Both call sites are in the platform-fallback branch of a UUID/random-byte generator; Linux and Windows both take dedicated CSPRNG paths above this branch, so the fallback (and therefore the missing API) is only reachable on other targets such as macOS.
resolution: Replaced std.time.nanoTimestamp() at both call sites with a portable seed: a per-process monotonically-increasing atomic counter (std.atomic.Value(u64)) mixed with std.Thread.getCurrentId() and the destination buffer's address. No timestamp or Io instance is needed. Verified: zig build, zig build test, and cross-compile for x86_64-macos, aarch64-macos, x86_64-linux-gnu, aarch64-linux-gnu all exit 0.
acceptance_criteria: zig build -Dtarget=aarch64-macos exits 0 (not yet checked either way)
acceptance_criteria_status: Both met — verified via zig build -Dtarget=x86_64-macos and -Dtarget=aarch64-macos, both exit 0 with no output.
